name: see_if
title: Assert that certain conditions are true.

origin.description: see_if returns the assertion instead of stopping.

arguments.text: Unnamed expressions that describe the conditions.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: The environment in which to evaluate the assertions.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom message if one of the conditions is false.

origin.details: Returns TRUE, or FALSE with the failure message in the msg attribute. It catches assertError only. A bad assertion result still stops.
origin.value: TRUE, or FALSE with a msg attribute.
origin.example:
x <- 1
see_if(is.character(x))
see_if(length(x) == 3)
see_if(is.dir(17))
see_if(is.dir("asdf"))
see_if(5 < 3, msg = "Five is not smaller than three")

translation.description: see_if returns the assertion instead of stopping.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: A dict of names. When omitted, names come from the caller's locals.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom message if one of the conditions is false.

translation.details: Returns a SeeResult. Printed, it shows TRUE, or FALSE with the msg attribute. It catches AssertThatError only. A bad assertion result still raises ValueError. Expressions are strings.
translation.example:
from assertthat import see_if

x = 1
print(see_if("is.character(x)"))
print(see_if("length(x) == 3"))
print(see_if("is.dir(17)"))
print(see_if('is.dir("asdf")'))
print(see_if("5 < 3", msg="Five is not smaller than three"))
